response.query: What annotated corpus size, inter-annotator agreement targets (Cohen’s kappa/Krippendorff’s alpha), and out-of-sample metrics are recommended to validate ML classifiers of gendered language in pitches and profiles?
response.answer: For ML classifiers of gendered language, a corpus size of at least 1,000 samples is recommended, with inter-annotator agreement targets of Krippendorff’s alpha or Cohen’s kappa above 0.7, and out-of-sample accuracy metrics above 85%.

results.content: We present a freely available corpus containing source language texts from different domains along with their automatically generated translations into several distinct morphologically rich languages, their post-edited versions, and error annotations of the performed post-edit operations. In this paper we present a language resource for German, composed of a list of 1,021 unique errors extracted from a collection of texts written by people with dyslexia. In this paper we test the utility of the ISO standard through comparative evaluation of the corpus-specific legacy and the semi-automatically transferred DiAML DA annotations on supervised dialogue act[...]d to identify similar contexts. We have constructed a new speech data corpus, using the utterances of 100 elderly Japanese people, to improve speech recognition accuracy of the speech of older people. To create automatic transcription and annotation tools for the AHEYM corpus of recorded interviews with Yiddish speakers in Eastern Europe we develop initial Yiddish language resources that are used for adaptations of speech and language technologies.

results.title: Proceedings of the Thirteenth Language Resources and ...
results.content: The DGS Corpus is a large collection of recordings of members of the deaf community in Germany communicating in their primary language, German Sign Language (DGS); it was created to be both as a resource for linguistic research and as a record of the life experiences of deaf people in Germany. To assess its usefulness for training and testing ASR systems for Bemba, we explored different approaches; supervised pre-training (training from scratch), cross-lingual transfer learning from a monolingual English pre-trained model using DeepSpeech on the portion of the dataset and fine-tuning large scale self-supervised Wav2Vec2.0 based multilingual pre-trained models on the complete BembaSpeech corpus. We also introduce new annotated datasets useful for future research in Sinhala text classification and publicly release our pre-trained models. **[Pre-training and Evaluating Transformer-based Language Models for Icelandic](/2022.lrec-1.804/)**.
